core.title: Give every train a typed kebab-case identity
core.given: The change set contains a train definition document: a plan artifact whose purpose is to define one train (its own identity, title and contents), wherever it currently sits. Files that only reference trains, and non-train auxiliary files, are not train documents.
core.when: the planner creates, edits, renames or moves it, or changes its identity, title or file location
core.then: Set the train's identity to the stack's typed train URN, with both the subject and the descriptive-name segments in kebab-case.
prefer: Mandatory, not optional: store the train document flat at the stack's plan-item location for trains, with the filename taken from the train identity.
Mandatory, not optional: write the title in Title Case.
avoid: Untyped identities missing the train URN's type prefix or its subject segment.
camelCase, snake_case, spaces or uppercase in the subject or descriptive name.
Titles not in Title Case (e.g. lowercase or a copied kebab-case identity).
Nesting the train document in subdirectories below its plan-item location, placing train documents outside it, or a filename that differs from the train identity.
Renaming or adding train identity fields to README, registry or other non-train files.
core.why: A single typed, predictable identity gives each train one identity from which its file path and references can be derived mechanically.
evidence: Every train definition document sits flat at the stack's plan-item location for trains (no subdirectories, none elsewhere) and its basename equals its train identity.
Each train identity matches the stack's typed train URN with both segments kebab-case.
verification: Identity check: every train definition document's identity matches the stack's train URN shape (type prefix, subject segment, descriptive-name segment) with both segments kebab-case; the concrete matcher (e.g. a regular expression) belongs to the realization.
Title check: every train title is Title Case.
File check: every train definition document sits flat at the stack's plan-item location for trains, with basename equal to its identity — no subdirectories below it, none outside it.
One check covers the train identity, the title and the file naming together; the realization registers these under a single term id.

Candidate discovery belongs to the check: it scans plan artifacts anywhere under the plan root (including nested subdirectories of the train-document location); a candidate is a plan artifact that declares its own train identity per the stack's URN-declaration syntax; the check confirms the candidate's purpose is to define one train before applying the checks; files of other kinds and files that only reference train identities are skipped.
The rule declares no exceptions: the naming invariants hold for the whole document on every covered operation.

facts.note: Discovery signal only: plan artifacts under the plan root — in the train-document location (including nested subdirectories) or elsewhere under the plan root — are candidates. Path membership alone does not make a file a train document; README, notes and other non-train auxiliary files in that location are out of scope.
Train documents are files of the stack's plan-artifact kind; files of other kinds (e.g. a README) are never train documents.
Any change to a train document, including edits to non-identity fields; the naming invariants hold for the whole document.
Planning tasks that mention defining, editing, renaming or moving a train or its identity; the stack's local name for the identity field comes from the profile's URN-declaration syntax.

values: a candidate plan artifact declares its own train identity
facts.note: Content observer to surface candidates (including train documents misplaced outside or nested within the train-document location). A declared identity is a discovery signal, not proof: registries or files that merely reference train identities are not train documents.
Final classification: the candidate's purpose is to define one train (its own identity, title and contents), as opposed to an auxiliary, registry or reference-only file.

fires: Planner creates a new train definition document.
Planner edits any field of an existing train definition document, including only its title or only its wagon list.
Planner renames a train, changes its identity, or moves its definition file.
A train definition document sits in a subdirectory below its plan-item location, outside it, or under a filename that differs from its identity.
doesNotFire: Editing a README, notes or other non-train auxiliary file in the train-document location.
Editing a registry or other plan artifact that only references train identities without defining a train.
Editing wagons, WMBTs or acceptances without creating, editing or moving any train definition document.
Code or doc changes that contain no train definition document.

profileRequirements.meaning: The typed identity URN shape for trains, including the type prefix and the subject and descriptive-name segments that the rule requires in kebab-case.
profileRequirements.bunValue: train:{subject}:{descriptive-name}, with both subject and descriptive name in kebab-case

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of plan artifacts; the discovery scan covers plan artifacts anywhere under it, so train documents misplaced outside or nested within the train-document location are still found.
The file kind of plan artifacts; train documents are files of this kind, and files of other kinds are never train documents.

Path of one plan artifact under the plan root, used per its documented general meaning; for this rule it is the flat location and filename pattern of the train definition document, with the filename taken from the train identity.
How a plan artifact declares its own URN, used per its documented general meaning; for a train document this declaration is the content observer's discovery signal for candidate train documents.

neutralityNotes: Everything concrete was routed to the profile: the typed identity shape (urn.train), the discovery scan root (roots.plan), the plan-artifact file kind (suffix.plan_artifact), the train document's path (layout.plan_item, used for its documented general meaning 'path of one plan artifact under the plan root' — the stack's value for the train document is plan/_trains/{train_id}.yaml) and the train identity declaration syntax (urn.declaration, 'how a plan artifact declares its own URN' — here a top-level train_id field). No new profile keys are needed: the vocabulary's general plan-artifact keys cover the train case, and their WMBT examples are illustrative rather than exclusive assignments. kebab-case and Title Case are kept in the core as stack-neutral casing conventions (they bind to no runtime, framework or language). 'planner', 'train', 'wagon' and 'WMBT' are treated as neutral ATDD plan vocabulary rather than stack names. The exact detector regex and the term id train_naming have no neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly; the core's verification describes the same checks generically. Facts carry a 'note' field (beyond the minimal schema) to preserve the discovery-signal-only scoping semantics of the frozen rewrite.
